facts.text: A park with a museum and a boating lake, and events for children and families. No age is given.
facts.label: Park, museum and boating lake

evidence.quote: wandering around the museum or boating on the lake - there's plenty to enjoy at Gunnersbury.

facts.text: Which ages the park, museum and lake suit: not stated.
facts.note: No playground, and no age for any permanent activity, is described on the pages read.

facts.text: A network of tarmac paths; because the park is a natural environment, paths may be uneven in places.

evidence.quote: There is a network of tarmac paths within the park at Gunnersbury. However, because the park is a natural environment, paths may be uneven in places.

reviewReasons: not a fact type that may be accepted without a person

facts.text: A park toilet block near the museum, and a toilet in the museum.

evidence.quote: There is also an accessible toilet in the park toilet block, which is located near the museum.

facts.text: Accessible toilets in the museum (ground floor, no RADAR key) and the park toilet block.

evidence.quote: There is an accessible toilet in the museum. There is also an accessible toilet in the park toilet block, which is located near the museum.

facts.text: Baby changing: not stated on the pages read.
Ten minutes' walk from Acton Town (Piccadilly, District) or South Ealing; Kew Bridge rail; E3, 65 and H91 buses.

evidence.quote: Acton Town Tube Station Piccadilly and District lines Turn left when you leave the station and walk along Gunnersbury Lane for about ten minutes

facts.text: Two car parks, charged at all times: £1 for 30 minutes to 1 hour, £1 an hour after; Blue Badge holders free.

evidence.quote: There are two car parks available at Gunnersbury.

facts.text: Free designated disabled parking in both car parks.

evidence.quote: Designated disabled parking for blue badge holders can be found in both car parks and parking is free.

facts.text: The Pure in the Park café: weekdays 7am to 5pm, weekends 7am to 6pm.

evidence.quote: Café Monday to Friday: 7am to 5pm Weekends: 7am to 6pm

facts.text: A children's playground: not mentioned on the pages read.
facts.note: A large park is likely to have one, but nothing read says so.

facts.text: The museum lift serves all galleries and suits wheelchairs, including small motorised ones.

evidence.quote: Inside, a self-operated lift serves all the galleries and is suitable for wheelchairs, including small motorised ones.

facts.text: Step-free access throughout the museum (some ramps and slopes); a lift to all levels; a manual wheelchair to borrow.

evidence.quote: Step-free access is available throughout the museum, with some ramps and slopes

facts.text: Relaxed sessions every half term; quieter times are weekdays 2 to 4pm, weekend mornings 10 to 12.

evidence.quote: We offer Relaxed Sessions every half term.

facts.text: Park open daily from 7am until dusk; museum Tuesday to Sunday 10am to 4.30pm (closed Mondays).

evidence.quote: Opening Hours Museum Tuesday-Sunday 10am to 4:30pm Park Daily between 7am until dusk
